  <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Geist+Mono:wght@500;700;900&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;700&family=Inter:wght@400;500;600&display=swap" rel="stylesheet" />

  <style>
    /* =========================================================================
       THEME TOKENS — Graphite neutrals + locked peerd rainbow accents.
       ========================================================================= */
    :root {
      --base:    #101112;
      --inset:   #080909;
      --paper:   #F3F3EF;
      --white:   #FAFAFA;
      --cyan:    #00B7EB;
      --red:     #EF4444;
      --amber:   #F59E0B;
      --green:   #22C55E;
      --magenta: #D946EF;

      --panel:    #151617;
      --panel-2:  #1A1C1E;
      --secondary:#ABABA6;
      --muted:    #70716E;
      --hairline: #25272A;
      --hairline-strong: #32353A;

      --pad-h: clamp(20px, 5vw, 64px);
    }

    *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
    html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; }
    html { scroll-behavior: smooth; }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      html { scroll-behavior: auto; }
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       FOCUS-VISIBLE — keyboard a11y. Branded ring in cyan, only on
       keyboard focus (mouse clicks don't trigger). Matches the brand
       palette and is offset slightly to read as intentional design,
       not browser default.
       ========================================================================= */
    :focus { outline: none; }
    :focus-visible {
      outline: 2px solid var(--cyan);
      outline-offset: 3px;
      border-radius: 3px;
      transition: outline-offset 120ms ease;
    }
    /* CTAs already have their own border; tighten the offset so the ring
       doesn't fight with the button shape */
    .cta:focus-visible { outline-offset: 2px; }
    /* Wordmark links: offset enough to read against the colored blocks */
    .wordmark-link:focus-visible { outline-offset: 4px; }

    body {
      background: var(--base);
      color: var(--paper);
      font-family: 'Inter', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif;
      font-size: 15px;
      line-height: 1.6;
      min-height: 100vh;
      -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
    }

    ::selection { background: var(--cyan); color: var(--base); }

    /* =========================================================================
       LAYOUT
       ========================================================================= */
    .nav, .container {
      max-width: 1100px;
      margin: 0 auto;
      padding-left: var(--pad-h);
      padding-right: var(--pad-h);
    }

    .nav {
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: space-between;
      padding-top: 24px;
      padding-bottom: 24px;
      /*
        Sticky positioning so the nav remains pinned to the top of the
        viewport as the user scrolls. The crossfade (hero wordmark fading
        out, nav wordmark fading in) only "lands" if the nav slot is
        always visible while scrolling.

        Background matches page-base so the nav band visually merges with
        the body color on either side of the 1100px content rail — no
        visible left/right gaps from the max-width constraint.

        z-index 50 keeps the nav above all section content (highest other
        in-flow stack is 10, on the mobile menu).
      */
      position: sticky;
      top: 0;
      z-index: 50;
      background: var(--base);
    }

    .nav-links {
      display: flex;
      gap: 28px;
      align-items: center;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace;
      font-size: 12px;
    }

    .nav-links a {
      color: var(--paper);
      text-decoration: none;
      opacity: 0.7;
      transition: opacity 120ms ease;
    }
    .nav-links a:hover { opacity: 1; }

    /* =========================================================================
       WORDMARK — five colored blocks, big white letters
       --------------------------------------------------------------------------
       Font: Geist Mono (Google Fonts, free), weight 700 (Bold). Vercel's
       modern geometric mono. Significantly thicker than the previous Major
       Mono attempt, still mono, still geometric, lowercase coherent with
       uppercase. Reads as "control panel label" rather than "playful
       constructivist."

       Only the wordmark uses Geist Mono. Everything else stays in
       JetBrains Mono (headlines, code, labels) — keep the page typographic
       hierarchy clean: one display face, one workhorse face.

       No gap between blocks — reads as one solid unit. Outer corners
       rounded; inner edges square.
       ========================================================================= */
    .wordmark {
      display: inline-flex;
      gap: 0;
    }

    .wordmark .block {
      width: var(--size, 80px);
      height: var(--size, 80px);
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: center;
      font-family: 'Geist Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace;
      font-weight: 700;
      /*
        Letter ratio: 1.05 (em-box slightly larger than the block). At this
        ratio the letters fill the blocks edge-to-edge visually, with the
        descender on `p` and the ascender on `d` reaching very close to the
        block edges but not clipping. Pushing past ~1.1 starts to visibly
        crop descenders; if a more aggressive industrial look is wanted,
        that crop can be intentional.
      */
      font-size: calc(var(--size, 80px) * 1.05);
      color: var(--white);
      letter-spacing: -0.02em;
      line-height: 1;
      user-select: none;
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    /*
      Outer corners rounded; inner edges square so adjacent blocks abut
      cleanly. First and last block carry the rounding; middle blocks
      stay square.
    */
    .wordmark .block:first-child {
      border-top-left-radius: calc(var(--size, 80px) * 0.08);
      border-bottom-left-radius: calc(var(--size, 80px) * 0.08);
    }
    .wordmark .block:last-child {
      border-top-right-radius: calc(var(--size, 80px) * 0.08);
      border-bottom-right-radius: calc(var(--size, 80px) * 0.08);
    }

    .wordmark .b-p  { background: var(--cyan); }
    .wordmark .b-e  { background: var(--red); }
    .wordmark .b-e2 { background: var(--amber); }
    .wordmark .b-r  { background: var(--green); }
    .wordmark .b-d  { background: var(--magenta); }

    .wordmark--nav  { --size: 28px; }
    .wordmark--hero { --size: 60px; }

    /* =========================================================================
       WORDMARK TYPING ANIMATION (hero only) — two-phase
       --------------------------------------------------------------------------
       Sequence on page load (~1.76s total, after a 500ms initial breath
       so the page has time to settle before the animation begins).

       Phase 1 — letters type out, left to right (cursor leads).
         T=500    letter p appears; cursor advances to position 1
         T=620    letter e
         T=740    letter e
         T=860    letter r
         T=980    letter d
         T=1160   cursor fades out

       Brief breath (~120ms) — letters sit on the empty rail, no color yet.

       Phase 2 — blocks colorize, left to right (silent, no cursor).
         T=1280   p block fills with cyan
         T=1400   e block fills with red
         T=1520   e block fills with amber
         T=1640   r block fills with green
         T=1760   d block fills with magenta

       Both phases use 1ms "stamped" reveals on a 120ms cadence — same
       terminal-typing aesthetic in both halves. The split is what the
       eye registers: first the IDENTITY (letters), then the BRAND (color).

       Pure CSS. Plays once per page load. Respects prefers-reduced-motion.
       ========================================================================= */

    /* Only the hero variant is positioned to host the cursor + rail. */
    .wordmark--hero {
      position: relative;
      /* Crossfade transition (scroll behavior, wired in JS): hero wordmark
         fades+shrinks when the user scrolls past the hero, while the nav
         wordmark fades in. Visually: the wordmark "shrinks into" the nav slot. */
      transition: opacity 280ms ease-out, transform 280ms ease-out;
      transform-origin: top left;
    }

    .wordmark--hero.is-receding {
      opacity: 0;
      transform: scale(0.5);
    }

    /*
      The "empty rail" — a dark panel that fills the wordmark before any
      blocks have appeared. Visible behind transparent blocks during phase 1.
      Once blocks colorize in phase 2, they cover the rail. Once colorized,
      the rail is hidden behind the now-opaque colored blocks automatically.
    */
    .wordmark--hero::before {
      content: '';
      position: absolute;
      inset: 0;
      background: var(--panel);
      border-radius: calc(var(--size, 60px) * 0.08);
      border: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      z-index: 0;
    }

    /*
      During animation: block background is transparent (rail shows through),
      letter color is transparent (letter invisible). Per-block animations
      reveal letter (phase 1) and color (phase 2) at staggered times.
    */
    .wordmark.wordmark--hero .block {
      position: relative;
      z-index: 1;
      background: transparent;
      color: transparent;
    }

    /* Per-block staggered two-animation tracks (with 500ms initial breath). */
    .wordmark.wordmark--hero .block:nth-child(1) {
      animation:
        wordmarkLetterType 1ms       500ms forwards,
        wordmarkColorizeCyan 1ms    1280ms forwards;
    }
    .wordmark.wordmark--hero .block:nth-child(2) {
      animation:
        wordmarkLetterType 1ms       620ms forwards,
        wordmarkColorizeRed 1ms     1400ms forwards;
    }
    .wordmark.wordmark--hero .block:nth-child(3) {
      animation:
        wordmarkLetterType 1ms       740ms forwards,
        wordmarkColorizeAmber 1ms   1520ms forwards;
    }
    .wordmark.wordmark--hero .block:nth-child(4) {
      animation:
        wordmarkLetterType 1ms       860ms forwards,
        wordmarkColorizeGreen 1ms   1640ms forwards;
    }
    .wordmark.wordmark--hero .block:nth-child(5) {
      animation:
        wordmarkLetterType 1ms       980ms forwards,
        wordmarkColorizeMagenta 1ms 1760ms forwards;
    }

    @keyframes wordmarkLetterType      { to { color: var(--white); } }
    @keyframes wordmarkColorizeCyan    { to { background-color: var(--cyan); } }
    @keyframes wordmarkColorizeRed     { to { background-color: var(--red); } }
    @keyframes wordmarkColorizeAmber   { to { background-color: var(--amber); } }
    @keyframes wordmarkColorizeGreen   { to { background-color: var(--green); } }
    @keyframes wordmarkColorizeMagenta { to { background-color: var(--magenta); } }

    /*
      Cursor: tracks letter typing. Four concurrent animations:
        1. wordmarkCursorAppear — instant opacity 0→1 at t=500ms so the
           cursor doesn't render visible during the initial breath.
        2. wordmarkCursorStep — discrete jumps from position 1 to 5,
           in 5 steps over 600ms, starting at the 500ms initial delay.
           Uses steps(5, start) so the cursor advances AT THE START of
           each slice — meaning at the exact moment letter N types, the
           cursor lands at position N (right of just-typed letter).
           Previously used steps(5, end), which made the cursor lag one
           beat behind the letters.
        3. wordmarkCursorBlink — fast blink for terminal feel.
        4. wordmarkCursorFade — fades out at 1160ms (just after the last
           letter at 980ms; cursor has stepped to position 5 by 980ms with
           steps(5, start)).
      The cursor is gone before phase 2 (colorize) begins, so the colorize
      half plays in silence — no cursor, just blocks filling with color.
    */
    .wordmark-cursor {
      position: absolute;
      top: 8%;
      bottom: 8%;
      left: 0;
      width: 3px;
      background: var(--white);
      z-index: 2;
      pointer-events: none;
      opacity: 0;
      transform: translateX(0);
      animation:
        wordmarkCursorAppear 1ms   500ms forwards,
        wordmarkCursorStep   600ms 500ms steps(5, start) forwards,
        wordmarkCursorBlink  0.4s  500ms steps(2, end) infinite,
        wordmarkCursorFade   240ms 1160ms forwards;
    }

    @keyframes wordmarkCursorAppear {
      to { opacity: 1; }
    }
    @keyframes wordmarkCursorStep {
      from { transform: translateX(0); }
      to   { transform: translateX(calc(var(--size, 60px) * 5)); }
    }
    @keyframes wordmarkCursorBlink {
      0%, 50%      { opacity: 1; }
      50.01%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes wordmarkCursorFade {
      to { opacity: 0; visibility: hidden; }
    }

    /*
      Reduced-motion: skip both phases of the animation. Show the final
      state immediately — all blocks visible, fully colored. Same end
      result, just no animation getting there.
    */
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      .wordmark--hero::before { display: none; }
      .wordmark.wordmark--hero .block { color: var(--white); animation: none; }
      .wordmark.wordmark--hero .b-p  { background: var(--cyan); }
      .wordmark.wordmark--hero .b-e  { background: var(--red); }
      .wordmark.wordmark--hero .b-e2 { background: var(--amber); }
      .wordmark.wordmark--hero .b-r  { background: var(--green); }
      .wordmark.wordmark--hero .b-d  { background: var(--magenta); }
      .wordmark-cursor { display: none; }
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       NAV WORDMARK — scroll-driven emergence
       --------------------------------------------------------------------------
       Initially hidden (the hero wordmark is the only one visible on first
       paint). As the user scrolls past the hero, this one fades in and
       scales down from 1.3 → 1.0, which — paired with the hero wordmark's
       fade+scale-down — reads as the wordmark "shrinking into" the nav slot.

       The link wrapper is clickable to scroll back to the top.
       ========================================================================= */
    .wordmark--nav {
      opacity: 0;
      transform: scale(1.3);
      transform-origin: top left;
      pointer-events: none;
      transition: opacity 280ms ease-out, transform 280ms ease-out;
    }

    .wordmark--nav.is-emerging {
      opacity: 1;
      transform: scale(1);
      pointer-events: auto;
    }

    /* Footer wordmark — same visual treatment as nav but visible by default
       (no scroll-emerge behavior). Animation still triggers once when it
       enters the viewport, via IntersectionObserver. */
    .wordmark--footer {
      opacity: 1;
      transform: scale(1);
      pointer-events: auto;
    }

    .wordmark-link {
      text-decoration: none;
      display: inline-block;
      line-height: 0;  /* prevent extra spacing around the inline wordmark */
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       WORDMARK — typing animation (used by nav on first scroll-past, and by
       footer on first scroll-to). Selectors are deliberately generic
       (`.wordmark.is-typing`) so the same CSS drives both contexts.

       Compressed timing (60ms cadence). Sequence:
         T=0      letter p, cursor at position 1
         T=60     letter e, cursor at position 2
         T=120    letter e, cursor at position 3
         T=180    letter r, cursor at position 4
         T=240    letter d, cursor at position 5
         T=300    cursor fades
         T=360    p block colorizes (cyan)
         T=420    e block colorizes (red)
         T=480    e block colorizes (amber)
         T=540    r block colorizes (green)
         T=600    d block colorizes (magenta)
         T=700    JS removes .is-typing
       ========================================================================= */
    .wordmark.is-typing {
      position: relative;
      /* Override the crossfade transition while typing — we want INSTANT
         appearance, the typing animation IS the appearance. */
      opacity: 1;
      transform: scale(1);
      transition: none;
    }

    .wordmark.is-typing::before {
      content: '';
      position: absolute;
      inset: 0;
      background: var(--panel);
      border-radius: calc(var(--size, 28px) * 0.08);
      border: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      z-index: 0;
    }

    .wordmark.is-typing .block {
      position: relative;
      z-index: 1;
      background: transparent;
      color: transparent;
    }

    .wordmark.is-typing .block:nth-child(1) {
      animation:
        wordmarkLetterType 1ms       0ms forwards,
        wordmarkColorizeCyan 1ms   360ms forwards;
    }
    .wordmark.is-typing .block:nth-child(2) {
      animation:
        wordmarkLetterType 1ms      60ms forwards,
        wordmarkColorizeRed 1ms    420ms forwards;
    }
    .wordmark.is-typing .block:nth-child(3) {
      animation:
        wordmarkLetterType 1ms     120ms forwards,
        wordmarkColorizeAmber 1ms  480ms forwards;
    }
    .wordmark.is-typing .block:nth-child(4) {
      animation:
        wordmarkLetterType 1ms     180ms forwards,
        wordmarkColorizeGreen 1ms  540ms forwards;
    }
    .wordmark.is-typing .block:nth-child(5) {
      animation:
        wordmarkLetterType 1ms     240ms forwards,
        wordmarkColorizeMagenta 1ms 600ms forwards;
    }

    /* Cursor — 2px wide for nav/footer scale (vs 3px for hero). */
    .wordmark-cursor--nav {
      position: absolute;
      top: 8%;
      bottom: 8%;
      left: 0;
      width: 2px;
      background: var(--white);
      z-index: 2;
      pointer-events: none;
      opacity: 0;
      transform: translateX(0);
      animation:
        wordmarkCursorAppear   1ms    0ms forwards,
        wordmarkNavCursorStep  240ms  0ms steps(5, start) forwards,
        wordmarkCursorBlink    0.4s   0ms steps(2, end) infinite,
        wordmarkCursorFade     160ms 300ms forwards;
    }

    @keyframes wordmarkNavCursorStep {
      from { transform: translateX(0); }
      to   { transform: translateX(calc(var(--size, 28px) * 5)); }
    }

    /* Reduced-motion: skip typing for any wordmark, show final state. */
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      .wordmark.is-typing::before { display: none; }
      .wordmark.is-typing .block { color: var(--white); animation: none; }
      .wordmark.is-typing .b-p  { background: var(--cyan); }
      .wordmark.is-typing .b-e  { background: var(--red); }
      .wordmark.is-typing .b-e2 { background: var(--amber); }
      .wordmark.is-typing .b-r  { background: var(--green); }
      .wordmark.is-typing .b-d  { background: var(--magenta); }
      .wordmark-cursor--nav { display: none; }
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       SECTION COLOR SYSTEM
       --------------------------------------------------------------------------
       Each section declares a --section-accent on its <section> element.
       The label, accent glyphs, code-panel borders, and pull-quote borders
       within that section all read from --section-accent.

       Section assignments after the V1 restructure:

         hero  → cyan    (h1 accent — brand-default, the entry point)
         §01   → green   (what it is, what it isn't — the differentiators)
         §02   → amber   (why the browser — the insight / aha section)
         §03   → red     (security — opens with the threat we defend
                          against. Green/red glyphs inside the section
                          override section-accent — they have specific
                          meaning, not decoration.)
         §04   → magenta (what's next — forward-looking, matches the
                          wordmark's `d` and the P2P thesis)
         §05   → amber   (FAQ — reuses §02's amber. Far apart in the page.
                          Questions are "the insight section" tonally.)
         §06   → cyan    (install — CTA bookend, brand-default)

       Brand bookends in cyan (hero + install); the four content sections
       in between cycle through the brand colors. The FAQ reuses amber
       by design — see the note above.
       ========================================================================= */
    :root {
      --section-accent: var(--cyan);  /* default — overridden per section */
    }

    .label {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 12px;
      color: var(--section-accent);
      letter-spacing: 0.05em;
      margin-bottom: 32px;
      text-transform: lowercase;
      padding-left: 12px;
      border-left: 3px solid var(--section-accent);
      line-height: 1.4;
    }

    h2 {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-weight: 700;
      font-size: clamp(27px, 4vw, 43px);
      line-height: 1.15;
      letter-spacing: -0.015em;
      color: var(--paper);
      margin: 0 0 24px 0;
    }

    h3 {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-weight: 700;
      font-size: 17px;
      line-height: 1.3;
      color: var(--paper);
      margin: 0 0 12px 0;
    }

    p { margin: 0 0 16px 0; max-width: 720px; }
    p:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }

    .muted { color: var(--secondary); }
    .mono  { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; }

    section.block-section {
      padding-top: clamp(72px, 10vh, 120px);
      padding-bottom: clamp(72px, 10vh, 120px);
      border-top: 1px solid var(--hairline);
    }
    section.block-section:first-of-type { border-top: 0; }

    /* Per-section accent overrides. */
    section[data-accent="cyan"]    { --section-accent: var(--cyan); }
    section[data-accent="amber"]   { --section-accent: var(--amber); }
    section[data-accent="green"]   { --section-accent: var(--green); }
    section[data-accent="red"]     { --section-accent: var(--red); }
    section[data-accent="magenta"] { --section-accent: var(--magenta); }

    /* =========================================================================
       HERO
       Now leads with the platform thesis, with the wordmark + headline
       reinforcing rather than carrying the claim alone.
       ========================================================================= */
    .hero {
      padding-top: 7vh;
      padding-bottom: clamp(80px, 18vh, 160px);
    }
    /* Zone wraps the CSS wordmark + its high-res ANSI twin. The zone owns
       the hero spacing so the absolutely-positioned ANSI overlay matches
       the wordmark's footprint exactly (margins don't leak into it). */
    .hero .hero-wordmark-zone {
      position: relative;
      display: inline-block;
      margin-bottom: 70px;
    }
    .hero .hero-wordmark-zone .wordmark--hero { margin-bottom: 0; }

    /*
      High-res ANSI wordmark — hover easter egg.
      Generated client-side into this <pre>: the wordmark is drawn to an
      offscreen canvas, every pixel snapped to the brand palette, then
      emitted as ▀/▄ half-block glyphs (fg = top pixel, bg = bottom pixel
      — 2× vertical resolution per character cell, the classic ANSI-art
      technique). transform: scale() fits the natural text size to the
      CSS wordmark's exact box, so hover reads as "same logo, suddenly
      made of characters" rather than a layout jump.
    */
    .wordmark-ansi {
      position: absolute;
      top: 0;
      left: 0;
      margin: 0;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace;
      /* rendering substrate, not text — font-size must equal line-height
         or 1px seams open between half-block rows. Excluded from the
         site-wide type-scale tweaks. */
      font-size: 10px;
      line-height: 10px;
      letter-spacing: 0;
      white-space: pre;
      font-variant-ligatures: none;
      transform-origin: top left;
      opacity: 0;
      pointer-events: none;
      user-select: none;
      z-index: 3;
      transition: opacity 140ms ease;
    }
    .hero-wordmark-zone:hover .wordmark-ansi.is-ready { opacity: 1; }
    /* fade the CSS wordmark out while its ANSI twin is in — but never
       fight the scroll-recede state, which must stay dominant */
    .hero-wordmark-zone:hover .wordmark--hero:not(.is-receding) { opacity: 0; }
    .wordmark--hero.is-receding ~ .wordmark-ansi { opacity: 0 !important; }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      .wordmark-ansi { transition: none; }
    }

    .hero h1 {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-weight: 700;
      font-size: clamp(33px, 5.4vw, 59px);
      line-height: 1.08;
      letter-spacing: -0.025em;
      color: var(--paper);
      margin: 0 0 32px 0;
      max-width: 920px;
    }
    .hero h1 .accent { color: var(--cyan); }

    .hero h1 .accent-m { color: var(--magenta); }

    .hero .subhead {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: clamp(14px, 1.3vw, 16px);
      color: var(--secondary);
      margin: 0 0 40px 0;
      max-width: 720px;
      line-height: 1.5;
    }

    .hero .lede {
      font-size: clamp(16px, 1.6vw, 18px);
      line-height: 1.55;
      max-width: 640px;
      margin: 0 0 20px 0;
    }

    /*
      lede-mark — inline cyan highlight for the two declarative sentences
      ("The browser is the runtime." / "The browser is the hypervisor.")
      that anchor the lede paragraph. Same hue as h1 .accent so the eye
      reads them as members of the same brand-color family. Weight bump
      keeps them readable as emphasized without going italic (Geist's
      italic is uneven across weights).
    */
    .hero .lede .lede-mark {
      color: var(--cyan);
      font-weight: 500;
    }

    /*
      Screen-reader-only utility. Standard a11y pattern — content is in
      the DOM and accessible to screen readers, but visually hidden.
      Kept as a general utility even though the cycle that introduced
      it has moved.
    */
    .sr-only {
      position: absolute;
      width: 1px;
      height: 1px;
      padding: 0;
      margin: -1px;
      overflow: hidden;
      clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
      white-space: nowrap;
      border: 0;
    }

    /*
      lede-peer — the "peerd is your AI peer" tagline. Sits alone between
      the lede paragraph and the lede-punch line as its own beat. Italic
      Inter rather than mono — this is the human-voiced claim, not a
      technical one, and italic gives it pull-quote weight without
      requiring a different size jump.
    */
    .hero .lede-peer {
      font-size: clamp(17px, 1.55vw, 19px);
      font-style: italic;
      color: var(--paper);
      margin: 0 0 24px 0;
      max-width: 640px;
      line-height: 1.4;
    }

    /*
      lede-punch — the "day we disappear" punchline. Bigger than the lede
      body, mono, cyan. Sits between the lede paragraph and the // marks
      line; the visual weight signals "this is the line." Italic-feeling
      without actually using italic (which Geist Mono doesn't have at all
      weights and reads awkward in mono regardless).
    */
    .hero .lede-punch {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-weight: 500;
      font-size: clamp(15px, 1.4vw, 17px);
      color: var(--cyan);
      margin: 0 0 28px 0;
      max-width: 640px;
      line-height: 1.4;
      letter-spacing: -0.005em;
    }

    .hero .lede-emphasis {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: clamp(12px, 1.1vw, 13px);
      opacity: 0.75;
      margin: 0 0 48px 0;
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       CTAs
       ========================================================================= */
    .ctas { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center; }

    .cta {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-weight: 500;
      font-size: 13px;
      letter-spacing: 0.02em;
      padding: 14px 24px;
      border-radius: 4px;
      text-decoration: none;
      border: none;
      transition:
        background 160ms ease,
        border-color 160ms ease,
        transform 160ms ease,
        box-shadow 160ms ease;
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 8px;
      cursor: pointer;
    }

    .cta:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); }
    .cta:active { transform: translateY(0); transition-duration: 80ms; }

    .cta--primary {
      background: var(--cyan);
      color: var(--base);
      border: 1px solid var(--cyan);
    }
    .cta--primary:hover {
      background: #14C7FA;
      border-color: #14C7FA;
      box-shadow: 0 4px 14px rgba(0, 183, 235, 0.25);
    }

    .cta--secondary {
      background: transparent;
      color: var(--paper);
      border: 1px solid rgba(232, 230, 225, 0.25);
    }
    .cta--secondary:hover {
      border-color: var(--paper);
      box-shadow: 0 4px 14px rgba(232, 230, 225, 0.08);
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       SECTION 01 — what it is
       ========================================================================= */
    .what p { font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.6; }
    .inline-code {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      background: var(--panel);
      border: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      color: var(--section-accent);
      padding: 2px 8px;
      border-radius: 3px;
      font-size: 0.92em;
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       SECTION 02 — WHY THE BROWSER (the platform thesis)
       New section. Five points, each a one-liner that doubles as a hint at the
       roadmap without committing to dates. The order goes inheritance → DOM →
       hardware → local inference → P2P, which is roughly "biggest current
       advantage" to "biggest long-term advantage."
       ========================================================================= */
    .why-browser h2 {
      margin-bottom: 40px;
    }

    /*
      §02 h2 cycling noun — the word at the end of "The browser is the X"
      cycles through "runtime", "network", "hypervisor", "operating system"
      via a typewriter effect. The noun gets amber (the section accent) so
      the eye reads it as the dynamic element. min-width reserves space
      for the longest word ("operating system.") to prevent layout shift
      mid-cycle. Two of the four words (.italic class) render italic to
      signal the more conceptual/architectural pair.
    */
    .why-browser h2 .h2-cycle-noun {
      color: var(--amber);
      display: inline-block;
      min-width: 12em;
      text-align: left;
      vertical-align: baseline;
    }

    .why-browser h2 .h2-cycle-text.italic { font-style: italic; }

    .why-browser h2 .h2-cycle-cursor {
      display: inline-block;
      width: 3px;
      height: 0.85em;
      background: var(--amber);
      vertical-align: baseline;
      margin-left: 2px;
      animation: h2CursorBlink 0.6s steps(2, end) infinite;
      position: relative;
      top: 0.05em;
    }

    @keyframes h2CursorBlink {
      0%, 49%   { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }

    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      .why-browser h2 .h2-cycle-cursor { display: none; }
    }

    .why-browser .preamble {
      font-size: 16px;
      max-width: 720px;
      margin-bottom: 20px;
    }
    .why-browser .preamble:last-of-type { margin-bottom: 40px; }

    .browser-points {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
      gap: 32px;
      margin-top: 16px;
    }

    .primitives-intro {
      grid-column: 1 / -1;
      margin: 0 0 8px 0;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 12px;
      letter-spacing: 0.04em;
      color: var(--section-accent);
      opacity: 0.85;
    }

    /*
      Collapsible primitive cards.
      The card is a button-as-header (h3 + one-line teaser + chevron) plus a
      detail-wrap that animates open via the classic grid-template-rows
      0fr → 1fr trick — no fake max-height, content's natural height is the
      target, transitions correctly on resize.
    */
    .bp {
      display: flex;
      flex-direction: column;
      border: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      border-radius: 6px;
      background: var(--panel);
      transition: border-color 180ms ease, background 180ms ease;
      overflow: hidden;
    }
    .bp:hover { border-color: var(--hairline-strong); background: var(--panel-2); }

    .bp-head {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto;
      gap: 16px;
      align-items: flex-start;
      padding: 18px 20px;
      background: transparent;
      border: 0;
      width: 100%;
      cursor: pointer;
      text-align: left;
      color: inherit;
      font: inherit;
    }
    .bp-head:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--cyan); outline-offset: -2px; border-radius: 6px; }

    .bp-head .bp-glyph {
      transition: transform 200ms ease, opacity 200ms ease;
      opacity: 0.85;
      margin-top: 2px;
    }
    .bp:hover .bp-glyph { transform: translateX(2px); opacity: 1; }

    .bp-teaser {
      margin: 0;
      font-size: 12.5px;
      color: var(--secondary);
      line-height: 1.5;
    }

    .bp-chevron {
      align-self: center;
      display: inline-flex;
      width: 16px;
      height: 16px;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: center;
      color: var(--muted);
      font-size: 10px;
      transition: transform 280ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), color 180ms ease;
      transform: rotate(0deg);
    }
    .bp:hover .bp-chevron { color: var(--paper); }
    .bp--open .bp-chevron { transform: rotate(180deg); color: var(--paper); }

    .bp-detail-wrap {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-rows: 0fr;
      transition: grid-template-rows 320ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
    }
    .bp-detail {
      overflow: hidden;
      opacity: 0;
      transform: translateY(-4px);
      transition: opacity 220ms ease-out, transform 260ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
    }
    .bp--open .bp-detail-wrap { grid-template-rows: 1fr; }
    .bp--open .bp-detail { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); transition-delay: 80ms; }

    .bp-detail-inner {
      padding: 0 20px 20px 68px;
      font-size: 13px;
      line-height: 1.6;
      color: var(--paper);
      max-width: none;
    }
    .bp-detail-inner p { margin: 0 0 10px 0; }
    .bp-detail-inner p:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }

    /* Reduced-motion: no slide, snap open instantly */
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      .bp-detail-wrap, .bp-detail, .bp-chevron { transition: none; }
      .bp-detail { transform: none; }
    }

    /*
      Glyph for each browser-primitive point. Color is uniform per section
      now — they all use the section-accent (amber for §02). The visual
      rhythm comes from the grid, not from glyph-color rotation. The
      wordmark already does the multi-color work; sections stay disciplined.
    */
    .bp-glyph {
      flex-shrink: 0;
      width: 32px;
      height: 32px;
      border-radius: 4px;
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: center;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-weight: 700;
      font-size: 13px;
      color: var(--white);
      line-height: 1;
      background: var(--section-accent);
    }

    .bp h3 {
      margin: 0 0 4px 0;
      font-size: 15px;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-weight: 700;
      color: var(--paper);
      line-height: 1.3;
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       VM TERMINAL PANEL (in §02)
       Variant of the code-panel pattern, but visually mimics a terminal
       session — three dots in the header, a cyan prompt, a green path,
       a blinking cursor. Different look from the skill snippet so the
       two §02 panels read as different *things* (live shell vs config file).
       ========================================================================= */
    .vm-terminal {
      margin-top: 56px;
      background: var(--inset);
      border: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      border-radius: 6px;
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    .vm-terminal .head {
      padding: 10px 16px;
      border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 11px;
      color: var(--muted);
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 16px;
    }

    /* Three colored dots, palette-coherent. Red/amber/green from the
       wordmark — not the classic macOS traffic light, just our palette
       used at very small size. Decorative but on-brand. */
    .vm-terminal .dots {
      display: inline-flex;
      gap: 6px;
      align-items: center;
    }
    .vm-terminal .dot {
      width: 10px;
      height: 10px;
      border-radius: 50%;
      display: inline-block;
    }
    .vm-terminal .dot-r { background: var(--red); }
    .vm-terminal .dot-a { background: var(--amber); }
    .vm-terminal .dot-g { background: var(--green); }

    .vm-terminal .title {
      flex: 1;
      color: var(--paper);
      opacity: 0.85;
    }

    /* The /vm-demo/ iframe is the entire panel body now (no button, no
       placeholder pre). flex:1 inside .demo-strip's stretch column +
       min-height keeps the panel a reasonable size on tall screens.
       background matches the iframe's own page so the brief pre-load
       paint doesn't flash white. */
    .vm-terminal iframe {
      display: block;
      width: 100%;
      flex: 1;
      min-height: 360px;
      border: 0;
      background: var(--inset);
    }

    .vm-terminal .tag {
      color: var(--section-accent);
      font-size: 10px;
    }

    .vm-terminal pre {
      margin: 0;
      padding: 20px;
      overflow-x: auto;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 12px;
      line-height: 1.7;
      color: var(--paper);
    }

    /* Terminal-specific token colors. The prompt is cyan (the brand color
       and our "agent identity" color in chat). The path is green
       (affirmative, "you are here"). Muted2 is for non-essential
       punctuation like the colon and dollar sign in the prompt. */
    .vm-terminal .prompt { color: var(--cyan); font-weight: 700; }
    .vm-terminal .path   { color: var(--green); }
    .vm-terminal .muted2 { color: var(--muted); }

    /* Blinking cursor at the end of the session. Pure CSS animation.
       1.1s cycle, 50% duty (on half, off half). Stops respecting
       prefers-reduced-motion. */
    .vm-terminal .cursor {
      color: var(--cyan);
      animation: blink 1.1s steps(2, end) infinite;
    }
    @keyframes blink {
      0%, 50%   { opacity: 1; }
      50.01%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      .vm-terminal .cursor { animation: none; }
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       §02 DEMO STRIP — VM terminal + WebRTC peers panel, side-by-side, equal heights.
       Replaces the old terminal-on-top + skill-snippet-below layout, which was
       making the cards above look misaligned because the panels were stacked
       full-width instead of slotting into a clean two-up grid below the cards.
       ========================================================================= */
    .demo-strip {
      margin-top: 56px;
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
      gap: 24px;
      align-items: stretch;
    }
    .demo-strip > * { min-width: 0; }

    @media (max-width: 800px) {
      .demo-strip { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 24px; }
      .browser-points { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 16px; }
    }

    /* Override .vm-terminal's earlier margin-top inside the new strip — the
       strip itself provides the top spacing now. */
    .demo-strip .vm-terminal { margin-top: 0; height: 100%; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
    .demo-strip .vm-terminal pre { flex: 1; }

    /* =========================================================================
       PEERS PANEL — the LIVE p2p widget. /p2p/peers-widget.js joins this page to
       the real peerd lobby (wss://bootstrap.peerd.ai/rendezvous) as an ephemeral
       peer and renders everyone connected — website visitors and extensions — in
       the radial graph below. No simulation: real rendezvous, real WebRTC, real
       presence; it says so honestly if the network is unreachable.
       ========================================================================= */
    .peers-panel {
      background: var(--panel);
      border: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      border-radius: 6px;
      overflow: hidden;
      display: flex;
      flex-direction: column;
      min-height: 280px;
    }
    .peers-panel .head {
      padding: 10px 16px;
      border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 11px;
      color: var(--muted);
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 12px;
    }
    .peers-panel .head .conn {
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 8px;
      flex: 1;
      min-width: 0;
      overflow: hidden;
      text-overflow: ellipsis;
      white-space: nowrap;
    }
    .peers-panel .head .tag {
      color: var(--section-accent);
      font-size: 10px;
      flex-shrink: 0;
    }
    .peers-panel .status-dot {
      width: 8px;
      height: 8px;
      border-radius: 50%;
      background: var(--muted);
      box-shadow: 0 0 6px transparent;
      transition: background 240ms ease, box-shadow 240ms ease;
      flex-shrink: 0;
    }
    .peers-panel.is-connecting .status-dot {
      background: var(--amber);
      animation: peerStatusPulse 1.4s ease-in-out infinite;
    }
    .peers-panel.is-live .status-dot {
      background: var(--green);
      box-shadow: 0 0 8px rgba(34, 197, 94, 0.45);
    }
    .peers-panel.is-failed .status-dot {
      background: var(--red);
      box-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.35);
    }
    @keyframes peerStatusPulse {
      0%, 100% { opacity: 0.6; }
      50%      { opacity: 1; }
    }

    /* Live peer graph — the WebTorrent-style radial animation rendered by
       /p2p/peers-widget.js into #peers-graph. Mirrors the extension's network
       view: YOU at the hub (magenta, the d-for-distributed mark), peers orbiting
       a slowly rotating ring, each in a random brand color; a faint dashed edge
       = heard via gossip, a solid edge = a live WebRTC channel. */
    .peers-graph-mount {
      flex: 1;
      min-height: 0;
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: center;
      padding: 6px;
    }
    .pn-graph { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; max-height: 340px; }
    .pn-self { fill: var(--magenta); }
    .pn-self-ring {
      fill: none;
      stroke: var(--magenta);
      stroke-width: 1.5;
      opacity: 0.5;
      animation: pnSelfPulse 2.4s ease-in-out infinite;
    }
    @keyframes pnSelfPulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 0.25; } 50% { opacity: 0.6; } }
    .pn-self-label { fill: var(--paper); font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; }
    .pn-edge { stroke: var(--hairline); stroke-width: 1.5; }
    .pn-edge--faint { stroke-dasharray: 3 5; opacity: 0.55; }
    .pn-dot { stroke: rgba(11, 13, 14, 0.4); stroke-width: 1; }
    /* Extensions get a bright outline so they read distinctly from website peers. */
    .pn-dot--extension { stroke: var(--paper); stroke-width: 1.5; }
    .pn-label { fill: var(--muted); font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 9.5px; text-anchor: middle; }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .pn-self-ring { animation: none; } }

    /* =========================================================================
       SECTION 02 — what it is, what it isn't (4-up named-competitor diff)
       Identity paragraph + four comparison cards. Was old §03, now also
       carries old §01's content. Grid is 2x2 instead of 1x3 because
       four cards × three columns leaves an orphan; 2x2 is balanced.
       ========================================================================= */
    .diff-intro {
      font-size: 16px;
      line-height: 1.55;
      max-width: 720px;
      margin: 0 0 48px 0;
      color: var(--paper);
    }

    .diff-grid {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
      gap: 48px 40px;
      margin-top: 16px;
    }

    .diff-item .num {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 12px;
      color: var(--section-accent);
      margin-bottom: 16px;
      letter-spacing: 0.05em;
    }
    .diff-item h3 { margin-bottom: 16px; }
    .diff-item p { font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--paper); }

    @media (max-width: 800px) {
      .diff-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 48px; }
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       SECTION 04 — security
       Was §03. Same content; renumbered. Still the workhorse.
       ========================================================================= */
    .security-intro p { font-size: 16px; max-width: 720px; }

    .security-closer {
      margin-top: 48px;
      padding-top: 32px;
      border-top: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      font-size: 15px;
      line-height: 1.55;
      max-width: 720px;
      color: var(--paper);
    }
    .security-closer em {
      font-style: normal;
      color: var(--green);
      font-weight: 500;
    }

    .defenses {
      margin-top: 48px;
      display: flex;
      flex-direction: column;
      gap: 24px;
    }

    .defense {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: auto 1fr;
      gap: 20px;
      align-items: flex-start;
    }

    .glyph {
      flex-shrink: 0;
      width: 32px;
      height: 32px;
      border-radius: 4px;
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: center;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-weight: 700;
      font-size: 15px;
      color: var(--white);
      line-height: 1;
    }
    .glyph--green { background: var(--green); }
    .glyph--red   { background: var(--red); }

    .defense h3 { margin: 0 0 6px 0; font-size: 15px; }
    /* Small label between paragraphs inside a defense card — used in §03
       to visually break up the trifecta and egress-chokepoint cards into
       sub-claims without forcing a full h4 break. Matches the
       comment-style labels used elsewhere on the page. */
    .defense .sub {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 10px;
      letter-spacing: 0.05em;
      color: var(--section-accent);
      opacity: 0.85;
      margin: 16px 0 4px 0;
    }
    .defense .sub:first-of-type { margin-top: 12px; }
    .defense p + .sub { margin-top: 18px; }

    /* In-card cyan highlight — pulled out of red/amber section flow to
       call out a thesis-y phrase. Used in card 1 to land "browser
       platform development tackling untrusted code and content safety". */
    .defense .hl { color: var(--cyan); }

    /* Secondary "beat" paragraph inside a defense card — same width
       and alignment as the main paragraph, just a bit more top space
       so it reads as a separate related claim. */
    .defense .aside { margin-top: 14px; }

    /* Card link — high-contrast cyan instead of the default
       red-on-red-section + dotted-border combo, which reads as faded
       against the panel background. */
    .defense a {
      color: var(--cyan);
      text-decoration: underline;
      text-decoration-color: rgba(0, 183, 235, 0.4);
      text-underline-offset: 3px;
      border-bottom: 0;
      transition: text-decoration-color 160ms ease, color 160ms ease;
    }
    .defense a:hover {
      text-decoration-color: var(--cyan);
      opacity: 1;
    }
    .defense p { margin: 0; font-size: 14px; color: var(--paper); line-height: 1.55; }

    /* Code panel — egress allowlist excerpt */
    .code-panel {
      margin-top: 48px;
      background: var(--panel);
      border: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      border-radius: 6px;
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    .code-panel .head {
      padding: 12px 20px;
      border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 11px;
      color: var(--secondary);
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: space-between;
    }

    .code-panel pre {
      margin: 0;
      padding: 20px;
      overflow-x: auto;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 12px;
      line-height: 1.6;
      color: var(--paper);
    }

    /* Syntax token colors — all from the locked palette */
    .tok-comment { color: var(--muted); }
    .tok-string  { color: var(--cyan); }
    .tok-keyword { color: var(--magenta); }
    .tok-error   { color: var(--red); }
    .tok-fn      { color: var(--green); }

    .telemetry-callout {
      margin-top: 40px;
      padding: 20px 24px;
      border-left: 3px solid var(--green);
      background: var(--inset);
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 13px;
      color: var(--green);
      display: flex;
      flex-direction: column;
      gap: 6px;
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       SECTION 05 — what comes next
       Reframed to sell the vision. Five "Soon —" lines, monospace,
       directional but not date-committed.
       ========================================================================= */
    .future {
      text-align: left;
    }

    .future h2 { margin-bottom: 40px; }

    .future-block {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: clamp(16px, 1.8vw, 21px);
      line-height: 1.6;
      max-width: 760px;
      color: var(--paper);
    }

    .future-block .today {
      color: var(--paper);
      display: block;
      margin-bottom: 24px;
    }

    .future-block .soon-line {
      display: block;
      color: var(--paper);
    }
    .future-block .soon-line + .soon-line { margin-top: 8px; }
    .future-block .soon-tag {
      color: var(--section-accent);
      font-weight: 500;
    }

    /* Section-accent reading: every emphasis in the future-block uses the
       section color. The wordmark does multi-color work; the page sections
       stay disciplined. */
    .future-block .accent-line {
      color: var(--section-accent);
    }

    /* Prose paragraphs inside the future-block. The mono cadence of the
       Today/Tomorrow opener and the coda fits short lines; longer prose
       reads better in Inter. Sized down a step from the mono lines so
       the paragraphs feel like supporting text under the lead-in. */
    .future-block .future-prose {
      font-family: 'Inter', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif;
      font-size: 16px;
      line-height: 1.6;
      max-width: 680px;
      margin: 28px 0;
      color: var(--paper);
    }
    .future-block .future-prose:last-of-type {
      margin-bottom: 32px;
    }

    /* Standalone callout line — pulled out of the prose to give "the
       real web 3.0" its own visual beat between the paragraphs and
       the coda. Mono to match the opener and coda cadence; magenta
       (section accent) for prominence. */
    .future-block .future-tagline {
      display: block;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-weight: 500;
      font-size: clamp(19px, 2vw, 25px);
      color: var(--section-accent);
      margin: 8px 0 0 0;
      letter-spacing: -0.005em;
    }

    .future-block .coda {
      display: block;
      margin-top: 40px;
      color: var(--paper);
      font-weight: 500;
    }
    /* Coda emphasis: the climactic claim of §04. Color + weight
       + a fractional size bump to make it the loudest line in the
       three-line coda without breaking the manifesto cadence. */
    .future-block .coda .em {
      color: var(--section-accent);
      font-weight: 700;
      font-size: 1.08em;
      letter-spacing: -0.01em;
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       SECTION 05 — FAQ
       Top questions readers will ask. Two-column on desktop for fast
       scanning; single-column on narrower screens. Questions in
       section-accent color; answers in body color.
       ========================================================================= */
    .faq-section h2 { margin-bottom: 48px; }

    .faq-list {
      /* columns, not grid: rows pack independently per column so a short
         answer next to a tall one doesn't leave a dead gap (no row-height
         coupling). break-inside keeps each Q+A together. */
      column-count: 2;
      column-gap: 56px;
      margin-bottom: 40px;
    }

    .faq-row {
      max-width: 540px;
      break-inside: avoid;
      margin: 0 0 40px 0;
    }

    .faq-section .faq-q {
      font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif;
      font-size: 15px;
      font-weight: 600;
      color: var(--section-accent);
      margin: 0 0 12px 0;
      line-height: 1.4;
    }

    .faq-section .faq-a {
      font-size: 14px;
      line-height: 1.6;
      color: var(--paper);
      margin: 0;
    }

    .faq-section .faq-a a {
      color: var(--paper);
      text-decoration: underline;
      text-decoration-color: rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.4);
      text-underline-offset: 3px;
      transition: text-decoration-color 160ms ease;
    }
    .faq-section .faq-a a:hover {
      text-decoration-color: var(--section-accent);
    }

    .faq-more {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 12px;
      color: var(--muted);
      margin: 32px 0 0 0;
    }
    .faq-more a {
      color: var(--paper);
      text-decoration: underline;
      text-decoration-color: var(--hairline);
      text-underline-offset: 3px;
    }
    .faq-more a:hover {
      text-decoration-color: var(--cyan);
    }

    @media (max-width: 800px) {
      .faq-list { column-count: 1; }
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       SECTION 06 — install
       Tabbed installer: chrome / firefox / github. Each panel has a
       short pitch line, the CTA, and a meta line below.
       ========================================================================= */
    .install h2 { margin-bottom: 16px; }

    .install .pitch {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 13px;
      color: var(--muted);
      max-width: 600px;
      margin-bottom: 32px;
    }

    .install-tabs {
      display: flex;
      gap: 4px;
      border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      margin-bottom: 32px;
    }

    .install-tab {
      background: none;
      border: none;
      color: var(--muted);
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 13px;
      padding: 12px 20px;
      cursor: pointer;
      border-bottom: 2px solid transparent;
      margin-bottom: -1px;
      transition: color 160ms ease, border-color 160ms ease;
    }
    .install-tab:hover { color: var(--paper); }
    .install-tab.is-active {
      color: var(--cyan);
      border-bottom-color: var(--cyan);
    }

    .install-panel { display: none; }
    .install-panel.is-active { display: block; }

    /* platform logo at the top of each install tab */
    .install-logo { display: block; height: 40px; width: 40px; margin: 0 0 20px 0; }

    /* hero "coming soon" row: muted metadata treatment, logos inline */
    .cta-soon {
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 10px;
      margin: 18px 0 0 0;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 13px;
      color: var(--muted);
    }
    .cta-soon .soon-logo { flex: none; height: 20px; width: 20px; opacity: 0.85; }

    .install-line {
      font-size: 18px;
      margin: 0 0 20px 0;
      max-width: 600px;
    }

    .install-meta {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 12px;
      color: var(--muted);
      margin: 20px 0 0 0;
      max-width: 640px;
    }
    .install-meta code,
    .install-meta a {
      color: var(--paper);
    }
    .install-meta a:hover { color: var(--cyan); }

    .install-code {
      background: var(--panel);
      border: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      border-radius: 6px;
      padding: 16px 20px;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 12px;
      color: var(--paper);
      overflow-x: auto;
      max-width: 720px;
      margin-bottom: 4px;
    }
    .install-code code {
      font-family: inherit;
      white-space: nowrap;
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       FOOTER
       ========================================================================= */
    footer {
      padding: 72px var(--pad-h) 32px;
      border-top: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      max-width: 1100px;
      margin: 0 auto;
    }

    .footer-top {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 12px;
      color: var(--muted);
      display: flex;
      flex-wrap: wrap;
      justify-content: space-between;
      gap: 24px;
      align-items: center;
    }

    .footer-marks { display: flex; gap: 16px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
    .footer-marks .ok { color: var(--green); }

    .footer-base {
      margin-top: 32px;
      padding-top: 24px;
      border-top: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 10px;
      letter-spacing: 0.04em;
      color: var(--muted);
      display: flex;
      gap: 12px;
      flex-wrap: wrap;
      align-items: center;
    }
    .footer-base .footer-sep { color: var(--hairline-strong); }
    .footer-base .footer-built { color: var(--muted); }
    .footer-base a {
      color: var(--secondary);
      text-decoration: none;
      transition: color 160ms ease;
    }
    .footer-base a:hover { color: var(--cyan); }

    .footer-credits {
      margin-top: 12px;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
      font-size: 10px;
      letter-spacing: 0.02em;
      color: var(--muted);
    }
    .footer-credits a {
      color: var(--secondary);
      text-decoration: none;
      transition: color 160ms ease;
    }
    .footer-credits a:hover { color: var(--cyan); }

    /* =========================================================================
       MOBILE NAV — hamburger toggle, CSS-only (checkbox hack)

       Pattern: a visually-hidden checkbox sits next to a <label> styled as
       the hamburger. Tapping the label toggles the checkbox; CSS sibling
       selectors flip the menu open/closed based on :checked state.

       No JS. Survives MV3 CSP. Accessible via keyboard (label is focusable
       and the checkbox state is the source of truth for assistive tech).
       ========================================================================= */

    /* Hamburger button — hidden by default, shown only at the mobile breakpoint */
    .nav-toggle { display: none; }
    .nav-toggle-label {
      display: none;
      cursor: pointer;
      width: 32px;
      height: 32px;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: center;
      border-radius: 4px;
      transition: background 120ms ease;
    }
    .nav-toggle-label:hover { background: var(--panel); }

    /* Three horizontal bars. Animated to an X when checked. */
    .nav-toggle-bars {
      position: relative;
      width: 18px;
      height: 12px;
    }
    .nav-toggle-bars::before,
    .nav-toggle-bars::after,
    .nav-toggle-bars span {
      content: '';
      position: absolute;
      left: 0;
      right: 0;
      height: 2px;
      background: var(--paper);
      border-radius: 2px;
      transition: transform 180ms ease, opacity 120ms ease, top 180ms ease;
    }
    .nav-toggle-bars::before { top: 0; }
    .nav-toggle-bars span    { top: 5px; }
    .nav-toggle-bars::after  { top: 10px; }

    /* Checked state — bars morph into X */
    .nav-toggle:checked ~ .nav .nav-toggle-label .nav-toggle-bars::before {
      top: 5px;
      transform: rotate(45deg);
    }
    .nav-toggle:checked ~ .nav .nav-toggle-label .nav-toggle-bars::after {
      top: 5px;
      transform: rotate(-45deg);
    }
    .nav-toggle:checked ~ .nav .nav-toggle-label .nav-toggle-bars span {
      opacity: 0;
    }

    /* =========================================================================
       Responsive: at <=640px, swap inline nav for hamburger panel
       ========================================================================= */
    @media (max-width: 640px) {
      .wordmark--hero { --size: 40px; }

      .nav-toggle-label {
        display: inline-flex;
      }

      /*
        Mobile nav-links: hidden panel below the nav bar.
        Slides down on open, full container width, mono links big enough
        to tap. Closed-state height = 0 so it doesn't push layout down
        when collapsed.
      */
      .nav-links {
        position: absolute;
        top: 100%;
        left: 0;
        right: 0;
        flex-direction: column;
        align-items: flex-start;
        gap: 0;
        background: var(--base);
        border-top: 1px solid var(--hairline);
        border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hairline);
        max-height: 0;
        overflow: hidden;
        transition: max-height 220ms ease;
        z-index: 10;
      }

      .nav-toggle:checked ~ .nav .nav-links {
        max-height: 320px;  /* large enough for all links */
      }

      .nav-links a {
        display: block;
        width: 100%;
        padding: 16px var(--pad-h);
        font-size: 13px;
        opacity: 0.9;
        border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      }
      .nav-links a:last-child {
        border-bottom: 0;
      }
      .nav-links a:hover {
        background: var(--panel);
      }

      /* No position override needed here — sticky on .nav (in the main
         rule) already acts as a positioning ancestor for the absolute
         .nav-links panel. */

      /* Install section: tabs row may need to scroll horizontally if
         labels wrap; install code block already has overflow-x. */
      .install-tabs {
        overflow-x: auto;
        flex-wrap: nowrap;
        -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;
      }
      .install-tab {
        padding: 12px 16px;
        white-space: nowrap;
      }

      /* Cycling noun: at narrow screens the h2 font is smaller (clamp),
         so we still need to reserve room for "operating system." but a
         little less than at desktop. */
      .why-browser h2 .h2-cycle-noun {
        min-width: 11em;
      }

      /* FAQ rows tighten up — narrow screens make 40px gaps feel too airy */
      .faq-row { margin-bottom: 28px; }

      /* Hero CTAs stack full-width for tap targets */
      .ctas { width: 100%; }
      .cta {
        width: 100%;
        justify-content: center;
      }
    }

        <h2>Native & cloud AI apps drive your browser from outside.<br/><span style="color: var(--section-accent)">peerd lives inside it.</span></h2>

        <p class="diff-intro">
          peerd lives entirely in your browser runtime: no background
          process on your machine, no sidecar, no cloud server, no external
          tool broker between the agent and the browser. Just you, your
          browser, and uncompiled, readable JavaScript.
        </p>

        <div class="diff-grid">
          <div class="diff-item">
            <div class="num">01.</div>
            <h3>Not an AI browser you switch to.</h3>
            <p>
              Comet, Atlas, and Dia are whole new browsers that ask you to
              move in. peerd is an extension: it adds the agent to the
              browser you already use, with your tabs, sessions, and
              extensions intact.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="diff-item">
            <div class="num">02.</div>
            <h3>Not a browser-automation service.</h3>
            <p>
              Playwright MCP, Browserbase, and cloud operators drive a
              separate, headless browser with none of your real session
              state. peerd <em>is</em> the browser you already use; agent
              and page share one process, on your machine.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="diff-item">
            <div class="num">03.</div>
            <h3>Not an MCP gateway with a browser attached.</h3>
            <p>
              peerd doesn't broker browser control through a cloud tool
              server. The browser itself is the harness; MCP is optional
              interop, not the architecture.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="diff-item">
            <div class="num">04.</div>
            <h3>Not a terminal coding agent.</h3>
            <p>
              Claude Code, OpenCode, and Aider live in your terminal. They
              can't see the page you're looking at, fill the form on your
              screen, or use the session you logged into. peerd can.
            </p>
          </div>

        </div>

      <!-- 03 — WHY IT'S DIFFERENT ======================================= -->
      <section id="why-browser" class="block-section why-browser" data-accent="amber">
        <div class="label">02, why the browser</div>
        <h2>
          The browser<br/>is the <span class="h2-cycle-noun" aria-hidden="true"><span class="h2-cycle-text"></span><span class="h2-cycle-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span></span>
          <span class="sr-only">runtime, the network, the hypervisor, and the operating system.</span>
        </h2>

        <p class="preamble">
          The first generation of agents lived in chat boxes. The second
          lives in IDEs, terminals, and cloud sandboxes. peerd is betting the
          next agent runtime is the browser itself: the place where you
          already have your apps, sessions, documents, permissions, identity,
          and workflows. peerd doesn't put an agent <em>near</em> the browser.
          It makes the browser the harness.
        </p>
        <p class="preamble">
          peerd uses the browser as its runtime, hypervisor, and security
          model. <strong>Zero lines of cryptographic code. Zero lines of
          sandboxing code. Zero lines of process-isolation code.</strong> The
          browser already wrote them, and hardened them for decades against
          the open web.
        </p>
        <p class="preamble">
          The agent control plane, permissions, audit, storage, and execution
          environment all live in the browser; models can be local or remote,
          your choice. That's the bet: the browser and the open web are the
          natural infrastructure for an ecosystem of open AI agents, already
          on every machine.
        </p>

        <p class="primitives-intro">// the agent workstation has five primitives:</p>
        <p class="preamble"><strong>Act.</strong> Use tabs, sessions, pages, and web apps through mediated browser tools.</p>
        <p class="preamble"><strong>Think.</strong> Route models, spawn subagents, use memory, plan, review, and operate under budget and permission limits.</p>
        <p class="preamble"><strong>Compute.</strong> Run notebooks, JS workers, compiled WASI tools, and Linux VMs in WebAssembly.</p>
        <p class="preamble"><strong>Build.</strong> Create artifacts, local apps, and reusable workflows.</p>
        <p class="preamble"><strong>Share.</strong> Connect browser agents peer-to-peer for A2A discovery, capability exchange, and signed app/workflow sharing.</p>

        <div class="browser-points">
          <p class="primitives-intro">// peerd inherits:</p>
          <!--
            Six collapsible primitive cards. Each shows just a one-line
            teaser by default; click anywhere on the card header to expand
            the full detail. Equal teaser lengths → cards line up cleanly
            in the 2×3 grid. Open state animates via grid-template-rows

          -->

          <!-- 1 — sandbox inheritance -->
          <div class="bp">
            <button class="bp-head" aria-expanded="false">
              <div class="bp-glyph" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
              <div>
                <h3>The V8 isolate.</h3>
                <p class="bp-teaser">The same primitive Cloudflare uses for their AI agent sandboxes at scale. Already in every Chromium browser, for free.</p>
              </div>
              <div class="bp-chevron" aria-hidden="true">▾</div>
            </button>
            <div class="bp-detail-wrap">
              <div class="bp-detail">
                <div class="bp-detail-inner">
                  <p>
                    Run them locally, for free, with no latency. <em>Firefox
                    exposes the same primitive through SpiderMonkey Realms;
                    peerd works with both. Millisecond start times,
                    configurable from HTML & OPFS exposure to WASM.</em>
                  </p>
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>

          <!-- 2 — Linux VM (security specifics moved to §03 egress chokepoint) -->
          <div class="bp">
            <button class="bp-head" aria-expanded="false">
              <div class="bp-glyph" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
              <div>
                <h3>A Linux VM, via WebAssembly.</h3>
                <p class="bp-teaser">A real Debian in a tab. The agent gets POSIX, inside the same sandbox as everything else.</p>
              </div>
              <div class="bp-chevron" aria-hidden="true">▾</div>
            </button>
            <div class="bp-detail-wrap">
              <div class="bp-detail">
                <div class="bp-detail-inner">
                  <p>
                    Not a remote shell. Not a fake terminal. A real Linux VM
                    compiled to WebAssembly, running in a tab, inheriting the
                    tab's enhanced isolation layered on top of the V8
                    isolate. The agent can run any command in it,
                    including destructive ones. The worst case is the VM
                    breaks and you start a new one. Your home directory is
                    not in the threat model. Each VM is its own tab: own
                    context, watchable, killable, attachable from any chat
                    session. Spin up several in parallel; the agent
                    addresses them by label.
                  </p>
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>

          <!-- 3 — sessions + DOM -->
          <div class="bp">
            <button class="bp-head" aria-expanded="false">
              <div class="bp-glyph" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
              <div>
                <h3>Your sessions, your DOM.</h3>
                <p class="bp-teaser">The agent inherits your logins and reads pages like the browser does.</p>
              </div>
              <div class="bp-chevron" aria-hidden="true">▾</div>
            </button>
            <div class="bp-detail-wrap">
              <div class="bp-detail">
                <div class="bp-detail-inner">
                  <p>
                    No OAuth dance, no credential storage, no session pools.
                    The DOM is to peerd what LSP is to a coding agent:
                    accessibility tree, mutation observers, ARIA roles,
                    computed styles, real cookies, real headers. Semantic
                    structure, not scraped HTML.
                  </p>
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>

          <!-- 4 — WebRTC -->
          <div class="bp">
            <button class="bp-head" aria-expanded="false">
              <div class="bp-glyph" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
              <div>
                <h3>WebRTC. The peer-to-peer network.</h3>
                <p class="bp-teaser">The peer-to-peer protocol built into every browser, on billions of devices. peerd uses it for agent-to-agent (A2A) coordination.</p>
              </div>
              <div class="bp-chevron" aria-hidden="true">▾</div>
            </button>
            <div class="bp-detail-wrap">
              <div class="bp-detail">
                <div class="bp-detail-inner">
                  <p>
                    The <em>d</em> in peerd is for distributed. peerd runs a
                    real browser-to-browser network
